title: Project infra — Vite, React, TypeScript, Vitest
description:
## Parent

shelf-proving-ground-513 (Fixture system)

## What to build

The minimal project infrastructure so that downstream tickets can build and test. After this ticket:

- `npm run dev` starts a Vite dev server serving an empty React app (a single root component rendering nothing meaningful).
- `npm run typecheck` runs `tsc --noEmit` against app and test files.
- `npm run test` runs Vitest.
- `tsconfig.json`, `vite.config.ts`, and `vitest.config` are in place.
- React, ReactDOM, TypeScript, Vite, and Vitest are installed as dependencies.

No app code, no components, no data layer — just the empty shell and working toolchain.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `npm run dev` starts successfully and serves an HTML page with a React root
- [ ] `npm run typecheck` passes with zero errors
- [ ] `npm run test` runs Vitest (can pass with zero test files or a trivial smoke test)
- [ ] `npm run lint` works (ESLint configured for TypeScript + React)
- [ ] package.json scripts match the commands table in CLAUDE.md

## Blocked by

- None (can start immediately).

title: App toolchain
description:
## What to build

Set up the Vite + React + TypeScript + Vitest development toolchain so that downstream tickets can write `.ts` and `.tsx` files, run unit tests, and serve the app in the browser.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `package.json` has `react`, `react-dom`, `vite`, `typescript`, `vitest`, and their type packages as dependencies
- [ ] `tsconfig.json` exists with strict mode, JSX support, and path resolution for `src/`
- [ ] `vite.config.ts` exists with React plugin configured
- [ ] `vitest.config.ts` exists (or vitest config in `vite.config.ts`) and `npm test` runs Vitest
- [ ] `index.html` exists at project root with a `#root` mount point and a script tag pointing to `src/main.tsx`
- [ ] `src/main.tsx` exists with a minimal React render (empty `<App />` component) — enough to confirm the pipeline works
- [ ] `npm run dev` starts the Vite dev server and shows the app in the browser
- [ ] `npm run typecheck` passes with no errors
- [ ] Existing `src/styles/tokens.css` is preserved and importable

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately).

title: Error state
description: Full-page error screen with message and Try Again button (reloads shelf), shown when fixture=error. Exercises error state pattern, retry flow, and distinct screen layout.

title: Empty state
description: Full-page centered illustration/message with CTA to add first book, shown when shelf has zero books. Exercises empty state pattern, CTA interaction, and responsive centering.

title: FAB
description: Floating action button in bottom-right corner that opens Drawer in Add mode. Hidden when Drawer is open. Exercises z-index layering, mobile safe-area insets, and conditional visibility.

title: Drawer
description: Modal dialog panel (right on desktop, bottom sheet mobile max ~70vh) with Add mode (empty fields, title focused) and Detail mode (pre-filled fields, segmented status control, inline delete with confirm/cancel). Immediate saves, close via X/click-outside/swipe-down/Escape, focus trap with aria-modal, slide animation, aria-live announcements for mutations. Exercises focus management, responsive panel layout, motion, and accessibility.

title: Book card
description: Card component showing title (2-line truncate), author (1-line truncate), and status badge (colored pill, top-right). Tap to open Drawer. Full keyboard navigation (tab between cards, Enter/Space to open). Exercises truncation, dark mode token usage, and accessible focus rings.

title: Shelf grid
description: Fluid responsive card grid displaying all books with filter chips (multi-select with All default), newest-first order, staggered card fade-in animation on load/filter change, and skeleton loading state (6 placeholders). Exercises responsive layout (1-4 columns), CSS grid auto-fill/minmax, dark mode theming, and animation.

title: Fixture system
description:
## Problem Statement

The app has no data layer. Components have nothing to call for books — no way to fetch, add, update, or delete. Without this, no UI feature can be built: the shelf grid, cards, drawer, and FAB all depend on a working API. There is also no mechanism to put the app into deterministic test states (empty shelf, error, slow network, truncation stress, scroll stress), which blocks all Playwright and screenshot testing.

## Solution

An in-memory data layer exposed as plain async functions, with a fixture system that switches the data and behavior profile via the `?fixture=` URL parameter. The API is the single source of truth for book state during a session. Fixtures make every UI state inspectable, screenshottable, and testable without randomness or external dependencies.

## User Stories

1. As a component author, I want to call `getBooks()` and receive a `Book[]`, so that I can render the shelf grid without managing data fetching myself.
2. As a component author, I want to call `addBook(title, author?)` and receive the created `Book`, so that I can immediately update the grid without re-fetching.
3. As a component author, I want to call `updateStatus(id, status)` and receive the updated `Book`, so that I can reflect the status change in the UI instantly.
4. As a component author, I want to call `deleteBook(id)` and receive void, so that I can remove the card from the grid with confidence the book is gone.
5. As a component author, I want `addBook` to reject an empty (or whitespace-only) title with a thrown Error, so that I can trust the data layer enforces the minimum contract.
6. As a component author, I want `getBooks()` to return books newest-first, so that I can render insertion order without sorting in the UI.
7. As a Playwright test, I want to navigate to `?fixture=empty` and see zero books returned by `getBooks()`, so that I can test the empty-state UI.
8. As a Playwright test, I want to navigate to `?fixture=error` and have every API call throw, so that I can test the full-page error state and retry button.
9. As a Playwright test, I want to navigate to `?fixture=slow` and have every API call take 2 seconds, so that I can test skeleton loading and pending states on all operations.
10. As a Playwright test, I want to navigate to `?fixture=long` and get 5–8 books with absurdly long titles and authors, so that I can test truncation behavior and take stable screenshots.
11. As a Playwright test, I want to navigate to `?fixture=many` and get 200 deterministic books, so that I can test grid scroll performance and filter counts.
12. As a Playwright test, I want the default (no `?fixture=` param) to return 5–8 seed books across all three statuses with hardcoded UUIDs, so that screenshots are stable across runs.
13. As a Vitest unit test, I want to call `initApi("fixture-name")` to reset the store to any fixture, so that I can test each API function in isolation with known state.
14. As a Vitest unit test, I want to call `initApi()` between tests to get a clean default state, so that tests are isolated without module-reimport hacks.
15. As a developer, I want the fixture name read once at module init from the URL param, so that I don't need to pass configuration through React context or props.
16. As a developer, I want the `many` fixture to use deterministic IDs (UUID pattern derived from index), so that screenshots are stable without a random seed.
17. As a developer, I want the `many` fixture to cycle statuses (`i % 3`), so that filter-by-status tests can predict exact counts.
18. As a developer, I want the `long` fixture to include edge cases — one very long word (no wrap points), many short words, multi-author strings — so that truncation stress covers real failure modes.

## Implementation Decisions

- **Plain async functions, not hooks or classes.** The API surface is 4 functions (`getBooks`, `addBook`, `updateStatus`, `deleteBook`) plus `initApi` for test setup. Framework-agnostic — React hooks are a separate consumer layer.
- **Two files: `api.ts` and `fixtures.ts`, flat in `src/`.** `api.ts` owns the functions, types (`Book`, `Status`), and the in-memory store (a module-scoped `let books: Book[]`). `fixtures.ts` owns the static seed arrays for each fixture name. No folder, no barrel.
- **Types co-located in `api.ts`.** `Book` is `{ id: string; title: string; author?: string; status: Status }`. `Status` is `"to-read" | "reading" | "finished"` (kebab-case). No additional fields — ordering is array position.
- **Author is optional** (`string | undefined`). A book can exist without an author.
- **Default status is always `"to-read"`.** `addBook` does not accept a status parameter.
- **`addBook` validates:** trim title, throw `Error` if empty after trim. No other validation.
- **`addBook` prepends** to the array (newest-first). `getBooks` returns the array as-is.
- **Mutations return the full `Book`** except `deleteBook`, which returns `void`.
- **Errors are plain `Error` objects.** No custom error classes.
- **Fixture read once at boot.** The module reads `?fixture=` from `URLSearchParams` on first import and seeds the store. `initApi(fixtureName?)` resets the store — used by Vitest tests. In the browser, auto-init happens; in tests, `initApi` is the entry point.
- **`error` fixture fails every call** (permanent error state). No retry-succeeds behavior.
- **`slow` fixture delays all calls** (fetch and mutations) by 2 seconds via inline `setTimeout` promise.
- **`many` fixture: deterministic loop.** 200 books: `"Book 001"` through `"Book 200"`, UUIDs from index (e.g., `00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001`), statuses cycling `i % 3`.
- **`long` fixture: 5–8 handpicked entries** with specific stress strings (long single word, many short words, multi-author).
- **`default` fixture: 5–8 seed books** with hardcoded UUIDs, all three statuses represented. Exact titles deferred to implementer.
- **IDs are UUID v4** — `crypto.randomUUID()` at runtime, hardcoded in fixture seed data.

## Testing Decisions

- **Single test seam: the public API of `api.ts`.** Unit tests call the 4 functions directly after `initApi`. No mocking of internals, no testing of array manipulation or fixture selection logic in isolation — test the contract, not the implementation.
- **Good tests exercise external behavior only:** call a function, assert the return value or the state observed via `getBooks()`. Never assert on the internal `books` array, import order, or module-level variables.
- **Vitest unit tests cover:**
  - Each function's happy path (add, get, update, delete)
  - `addBook` validation (empty title, whitespace-only title)
  - Ordering (newest-first after multiple adds)
  - Each fixture profile via `initApi`: correct count, correct IDs, correct statuses, error-throws, slow-delays
  - `initApi` reset (mutate state, re-init, verify clean)
- **Playwright tests are NOT in scope for this ticket.** The downstream UI tickets (grid, empty state, error state) will write Playwright tests that navigate with `?fixture=` and test through the rendered UI. This ticket provides the data layer they depend on.
- **Prior art:** The `e2e/support/` directory has Playwright helpers (`fixtures.ts` for console-guard, `ui.ts` for screenshot/motion/a11y). No Vitest config or unit tests exist yet — this ticket will establish the pattern.

## Out of Scope

- React hooks or context providers — consumer layer, not data layer.
- Persistence (localStorage, IndexedDB, backend) — explicitly in-memory only.
- Edit title/author mutation (`updateBook`) — spec only has status change and delete in Detail mode.
- Undo/redo.
- Retry-succeeds error fixture (`error-recoverable`) — may be added later as a separate fixture.
- Sorting or filtering — UI-layer concern, not API-layer.
- Vitest configuration (vite.config, vitest.config) — infrastructure ticket.

## Further Notes

This ticket blocks three downstream features: Shelf grid (`shelf-proving-ground-djk`), Empty state (`shelf-proving-ground-y4n`), and Error state (`shelf-proving-ground-2s9`). It should be completed first. The `Sandcastle` label marks it as ready for an AFK agent build.

title: Rewrite ui-foundation interview to use grilling pattern
description: The current interview produces navy blue by default because: (1) the template ships #2f6fed, (2) questions are linear not a design tree, (3) no stress-testing of answers. Fix by composing grilling into the interview, sanitizing the template, adding bias-check rules, and creating test cases.
close_reason: Rewrote interview to use grilling design-tree pattern, sanitized template colors, added bias-check rule, added test-cases.md, added no-default-colors rule
